channel.title: Fox's Blog (English)
channel.description: Fox3000foxy's blog about web development, automation, and open-source -- English

item.title: Luna Protocol: shared brains, emotion classification, and interesting/futile routing
item.description: Luna Protocol went from a monolith to a four-layer architecture: adapters, brain, emotion classifier, and inference. On the menu: embedding centroids, interesting/futile routing, and LLM parameter tuning by valence and arousal.

item.title: From ELIZA to LLMs: 60 Years of Conversational AI, Rebuilt in TypeScript
item.description: ELIZA, PARRY, ALICE, Jabberwacky, Cleverbot -- five radically different architectures for the same problem, ported to TypeScript with their original data. From 1966 to modern LLMs, here's how conversational AI learned to talk, and what a chatbot repo teaches us about 60 years of research.

item.title: Luna Protocol: Why I fine-tuned a 1.5B model on 50k Discord samples and why few-shot priming changed everything
item.description: A smaller model trained on less data can outperform a bigger one -- if you know how to prime it. Here is why Luna Protocol switched from a 3B Hermes to a 1.5B Qwen fine-tune, and why few-shot priming became the real game-changer.

item.title: How Machines Talk to Each Other: An Overview from TCP to mTLS
item.description: Why TCP, UDP, TLS, mTLS, HTTP, and WebSocket are not competing alternatives but stacked layers; a hierarchical overview of machine-to-machine communication, from raw transport to mutual authentication.

item.title: 5 ingenious ways to use GitHub Actions (and what they teach about secrets)
item.description: A CI runner turned into a free VPS, a bot that opens its own pull requests, an npm publish with zero secrets. A tour of my repos to catalog GitHub Actions patterns that go beyond "lint + test + deploy".

item.title: valorant-short-maker: the pipeline that generates my Valorant shorts by itself
item.description: Groq/Llama for the script, Piper for voices, FFmpeg for everything else. How a cron job produces and publishes one video a day on @valorant_agents, end to end.

item.title: How to get any cape on Minecraft Bedrock
item.description: A third-party launcher, an old version of the game, and a cape selector that never learned to say no. Full tutorial plus the likely explanation of why it works.

item.title: I evolved a neural network through natural selection instead of gradient descent
item.description: How I replaced classic gradient descent training with a NSGA-II genetic algorithm to evolve DQN trading agents: four versions, from overfitting to Lamarckian weight evolution.

item.title: TF2 Bots Aren't Random: I Reverse-Engineered Every Difficulty Setting
item.description: Vision, aim tracking, spy backstab angles, sniper headshot logic, every known bug -- Valve never documented any of it. So we dug through the code and turned it into a full spec sheet.

item.title: Cape Mod: how to steal Jeb_'s cape with RSA signature injection
item.description: A Fabric mod that exploits a logical flaw in Minecraft's trust system: a valid Mojang RSA signature but replayed on a wrong account. Code explanation, security implications, and cryptographic lessons.

item.title: Laupok built an AI that plays Super Mario World by itself -- how it works
Luna Protocol: I created an autonomous Discord bot that simulates a human being
item.description: Luna Protocol is a fully autonomous Discord bot powered by a local LLM, capable of natural conversation with sleep, typos, hesitations, forgetfulness, thematic fatigue, and spontaneous messages.

item.title: AI Learns Minecraft PvP -- Imitation Learning, Reinforcement Learning, and the 30 variables that mattered
item.description: 1,000 duels recorded, neural network trained on pixels, 90% keystroke accuracy : and the bot beelined into a wall. Then came RL, curriculum learning, and 60 hours of training.

item.title: Super Mario Bros.: the level format, pointers, and 256 glitch worlds
item.description: How 128 levels x 4 area types fit in 40KB of ROM, why the Minus World exists, and how a NES Tennis cartridge swap can load glitch worlds.

item.title: I spent a weekend reading konosuba-rpg's code and here's what I found
item.description: A turn-based Discord RPG where every action generates a WebP image on the fly: URL as game state, deterministic RNG, WASM pipeline, 5-level cache, serverless bot.

item.title: I built an ultra-realistic Express honeypot
item.description: 328 fake endpoints with on-the-fly generated responses, header spoofing, bot traffic logging -- a deep dive into an Express honeypot middleware designed to fool scanners.

item.title: Bareiron -- a Minecraft server running on a $1 microcontroller
item.description: 6800 lines of C, zero malloc, Perlin noise replaced by bilinear interpolation, biomes as a tile map -- here's the actual source code.

item.title: Discord bot 100% serverless: Hono + Cloudflare Workers
item.description: How I replaced a Discord bot that cost me 50€/month with zero euros -- interaction endpoints, Hono, Workers, real-time image rendering, and a full game without WebSocket.

item.title: My dumb AI for Nausicaa
item.description: A heuristic coefficient-based AI with hyperparameters that randomly change every 5 turns, and an Oracle that runs away -- diving into the brain of a mythological strategy board game.

item.title: Minecraft Pathfinding Logic and Applications
item.description: How A*, block malice, and POI mechanics let you control, predict, and exploit mob movement -- from wireless redstone to optimized farms.

item.title: UTAU: How a Visual Basic 6 app democratized synthetic singing
item.description: How UTAU, a free VB6 app from 2008, let anyone create synthetic singing voices with concatenative synthesis -- and why it still matters today.

item.title: Running a Node.js library in the browser without Wasm -- typescript-virtual-container's polyfills
item.description: How Fortune hand-rewrote node:fs, node:crypto, and a dozen more Node modules in 640 lines of JavaScript so the container runs in the browser without Wasm.

item.title: I used git as a database to run a bot for free on GitHub Actions
item.description: How I coded an AI email auto-responder that runs on GitHub Actions for 0€/month -- using git tags as a database and pre-compiled runtime snapshots.

item.title: Repo to VPS: Turn GitHub Actions into a free VPS with persistent storage
item.description: How to turn a GitHub Actions runner into an always-on VPS using git as persistent storage -- tmate, inotify, and commit --amend.

item.title: Comparing Javascript Solutions For Linux Kernels Simulation
item.description: A deep analysis of Linux environnements recreations in Javacript/Typescript.

item.title: Building character-factory: avatars with genetics
item.description: A TypeScript module on top of DiceBear: coherent country/ethnicity-based generation, a small genetics engine for projecting children, and the engineering details that made it usable in a card game.

item.title: Botting a Microsoft Rewards Farm
item.description: How I coded a bot to farm Microsoft Rewards points at scale -- and why Microsoft's anti-bot detection has since caught up.

item.title: Working on a New Project
item.description: A look at the process of starting and developing a new website.

item.title: About My GitHub Profile
item.description: A brief introduction to my GitHub profile.

item.title: My Passions
item.description: Coding, drawing, automating things, discovering old tech, and more -- a look into what drives me.

item.title: SSH commit signing script explained
item.description: A walkthrough of the SSH commit‑signing helper and why I wanted stylish commits.

item.title: How Does This Blog Work?
item.description: A deep dive into this blog's internals: React, Vite, Markdown, the CI/CD pipeline, and the article-writing workflow.
